theory.intro: A **composite solid** is built from simpler solids joined together — a barn is a rectangular prism with a half-cylinder roof, a bolt is a prism head on a cylindrical shaft, a drilled block is a prism with a cylinder removed. To find its volume, split it into the prisms and cylinders it is made from, find each volume, then **add** them (or **subtract** any part that is a hole). This is the skill that brings prisms and cylinders together.
facts: Split the composite solid into simple prisms and cylinders, find each volume, and **add** them; if a solid is a hole cut out, **subtract** its volume.
Prism $V = Ah$ (a box is $V = lwh$), cylinder $V = \pi r^{2}h$, half-cylinder $V = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$.
A cylinder's formula uses the **radius**; when a diameter is given, halve it first.
Keep the working exact and round only at the last line; capacity uses $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L and $1000$ cm³ $= 1$ L.
All lengths must be in the same unit before the volumes are combined.
steps: Split the composite solid into simple prisms and cylinders.
Find the volume of each simple solid.
Add the volumes, or subtract any that are holes.

foundation.solution_text:
Split the solid into a rectangular prism and a half-cylinder (roof radius $r = 3$ m).
$V_{\text{box}} = lwh$
$= 6 \times 4 \times 10$
$= 240\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{roof}} = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 3^{2} \times 10$
$= 141.3716\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 240 + 141.3716\ldots$
$= 381.3716\ldots$
$\approx 381.4\text{ m}^{3}$

Split the solid into the rectangular prism base and the cylinder.
$V_{\text{base}} = lwh$
$= 8 \times 8 \times 3$
$= 192\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 6$
$= 75.3982\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 192 + 75.3982\ldots$
$= 267.3982\ldots$
$\approx 267.4\text{ m}^{3}$

Take the volume of the block and subtract the cylindrical hole (radius $2$ cm, depth $5$ cm).
$V_{\text{block}} = lwh$
$= 10 \times 6 \times 5$
$= 300\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{hole}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 5$
$= 62.8318\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 300 - 62.8318\ldots$
$= 237.1681\ldots$
$\approx 237.2\text{ cm}^{3}$

Split the solid into the two cylinders and add their volumes.
$V_{\text{lower}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 5^{2} \times 3$
$= 235.6194\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{upper}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 6$
$= 75.3982\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 235.6194\ldots + 75.3982\ldots$
$= 311.0176\ldots$
$\approx 311.0\text{ cm}^{3}$

Take the outer cylinder and subtract the inner cylinder (the hollow middle).
$V_{\text{outer}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 4^{2} \times 20$
$= 1005.3096\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{inner}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 3^{2} \times 20$
$= 565.4866\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 1005.3096\ldots - 565.4866\ldots$
$= 439.8229\ldots$
$\approx 439.8\text{ cm}^{3}$

Split the bolt into the square-prism head and the cylindrical shaft.
$V_{\text{head}} = lwh$
$= 4 \times 4 \times 2$
$= 32\text{ mm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{shaft}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 1.5^{2} \times 8$
$= 56.5486\ldots\text{ mm}^{3}$
$V = 32 + 56.5486\ldots$
$= 88.5486\ldots$
$\approx 88.5\text{ mm}^{3}$

Split the solid into the block and the cylinder.
$V_{\text{block}} = lwh$
$= 2 \times 2 \times 0.5$
$= 2\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 0.6^{2} \times 2$
$= 2.2619\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 2 + 2.2619\ldots$
$= 4.2619\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
Capacity $= 4.2619\ldots \times 1000$
$= 4261.9\text{ L}$

The cross-section is a ring, so the pipe's material has cross-sectional area $\pi(5^{2} - 3^{2})$.
$A = \pi(25 - 9)$
$= 16\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$320\pi = 16\pi \times h$
$h = \frac{320\pi}{16\pi}$
$= 20\text{ cm}$

development.question_text: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius $2$ m and height $8$ m standing on a square concrete slab of side $6$ m and thickness $0.5$ m. Find the total volume of the structure, in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Split the structure into the cylinder and the square slab.
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 8$
$= 100.5309\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{slab}} = lwh$
$= 6 \times 6 \times 0.5$
$= 18\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 100.5309\ldots + 18$
$= 118.5309\ldots$
$\approx 118.5\text{ m}^{3}$

Take the block and subtract both cylindrical holes (each radius $1.5$ cm, depth $4$ cm).
$V_{\text{block}} = lwh$
$= 12 \times 8 \times 4$
$= 384\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{holes}} = 2 \times \pi r^{2}h$
$= 2 \times \pi \times 1.5^{2} \times 4$
$= 56.5486\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 384 - 56.5486\ldots$
$= 327.4513\ldots$
$\approx 327.5\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text: Solid A is a cylinder of radius $4$ cm and height $10$ cm sitting on a cube of edge $8$ cm. Solid B is a single cylinder of radius $5$ cm and height $12$ cm. Using volumes correct to $1$ decimal place, decide which solid has the greater volume and by how many cm³.
development.solution_text:
Solid A: $V = 8^{3} + \pi \times 4^{2} \times 10$
$= 512 + 502.6548\ldots$
$= 1014.6548\ldots \approx 1014.7\text{ cm}^{3}$
Solid B: $V = \pi \times 5^{2} \times 12$
$= 942.4777\ldots \approx 942.5\text{ cm}^{3}$
$1014.7 - 942.5 = 72.2$
Solid A is greater, by $72.2$ cm³.

development.question_text: A cylinder of radius $2$ cm and height $h$ stands on a cube of edge $6$ cm. The total volume of the composite solid is $(216 + 20\pi)$ cm³. Find the height $h$ of the cylinder, in cm.

A block is a $9$ cm by $5$ cm by $6$ cm rectangular prism with a cylindrical hole of radius $2$ cm drilled through the $6$ cm depth. Dev found the volume by adding the cylinder to the block, getting $345.4$ cm³. Explain the mistake, then give the correct volume, in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
The cylinder is a hole, so its volume must be **subtracted** from the block, not added.
$V_{\text{block}} = 9 \times 5 \times 6$
$= 270\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{hole}} = \pi \times 2^{2} \times 6$
$= 75.3982\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 270 - 75.3982\ldots$
$= 194.6017\ldots$
$\approx 194.6\text{ cm}^{3}$

Split the shed into a rectangular prism and a half-cylinder (roof radius $r = 4$ m).
$V_{\text{box}} = lwh$
$= 8 \times 5 \times 15$
$= 600\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{roof}} = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 4^{2} \times 15$
$= 376.9911\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 600 + 376.9911\ldots$
$= 976.9911\ldots$
$\approx 977.0\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text: A concrete support column is a square prism standing on a cylindrical base. The cylindrical base is $1$ m in diameter and $1$ m high. The square prism is $10$ m long and its square base fits exactly across the diameter of the cylinder, so the diagonal of the square equals $1$ m. Find the exact side length of the square, then show the total volume is approximately $5.8$ m³.
mastery.solution_text:
Let the square have side $s$. Its diagonal is $1$ m, so by Pythagoras:
$s^{2} + s^{2} = 1^{2}$
$2s^{2} = 1$
$s^{2} = \frac{1}{2}$
$s = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ m}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 0.5^{2} \times 1$
$= 0.25\pi\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{prism}} = s^{2} \times 10$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times 10$
$= 5\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 0.25\pi + 5$
$= 5.7853\ldots$
$\approx 5.8\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text: A tank is a cylinder of radius $1$ m and height $2$ m sitting on top of a rectangular prism $2$ m by $2$ m by $1$ m, and the whole tank holds water. Water flows in at $200$ litres per minute. Using $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L, find how long it takes to fill the tank, in minutes, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
$V_{\text{prism}} = lwh$
$= 2 \times 2 \times 1$
$= 4\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 1^{2} \times 2$
$= 6.2831\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 4 + 6.2831\ldots$
$= 10.2831\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
Capacity $= 10.2831\ldots \times 1000$
$= 10283.1\ldots\text{ L}$
Time $= \frac{10283.1\ldots}{200}$
$= 51.4159\ldots$
$\approx 51.4\text{ minutes}$

mastery.question_text: A hollow pipe has an outside radius of $6$ cm and is $20$ cm long. The volume of the pipe material is $400\pi$ cm³. Find the inside radius of the pipe, in cm.
mastery.solution_text:
The pipe material is the outer cylinder minus the inner cylinder.
$V = \pi R^{2}h - \pi r^{2}h$
$400\pi = \pi \times 6^{2} \times 20 - \pi \times r^{2} \times 20$
$400\pi = 720\pi - 20\pi r^{2}$
$20\pi r^{2} = 320\pi$
$r^{2} = 16$
$r = 4\text{ cm}$
